metadata.description: Canonical registry of all clinical trials and dataset analyses decoded by CrisPRO for the Brenus Pharma engagement. Covers ATR/DDR (GLB), CEACAM5, IO CORE, IO Appendix, Historical Benchmarks, BreAK CRC-001, and GBM EscapeMap (L8). NOTE: GBM_ESCAPEMAP entries are computational dataset analyses (entry_type=DATASET_ANALYSIS), not clinical trials.

trials.drug: Berzosertib (ATR inhibitor) + gemcitabine
trials.primary_result: ORR 17% overall; RS-High subgroup ORR 40% vs. RS-Low ORR 5%
trials.failure_mode: RS-saturated patients (RS-High) are unresponsive to ATR inhibition; ITT diluted by non-responders
trials.notes: GLB trial #1. Delta DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED — direction mismatch (RS-High should be lower fit, not higher).

trials.drug: Adavosertib (WEE1 inhibitor) + gemcitabine
trials.primary_result: ORR 23% (PTEN-intact) vs. 0% (PTEN-loss); PFS HR 0.55 (PTEN-intact) vs. 1.82 (PTEN-loss)
trials.failure_mode: PTEN-loss bypasses WEE1 dependency → non-responders dilute ITT signal
trials.source_pmid: Lheureux et al. Clin Cancer Res 2021
trials.notes: GLB trial #2. Delta DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED — direction match TRUE.

trials.drug: Ceralasertib (ATR inhibitor) + olaparib (PARPi)
trials.primary_result: ORR 36% (PARPi-naive) vs. 4% (post-PARPi); PFS HR 0.42 (PARPi-naive) vs. 1.31 (post-PARPi)
trials.failure_mode: Post-PARPi efflux resistance → non-responders dilute ITT signal
trials.notes: GLB trial #3. Delta DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED — direction mismatch.

trials.drug: Ceralasertib (ATR inhibitor) + durvalumab (PD-L1)
trials.primary_result: STK11/KEAP1-loss subgroup showed benefit; STK11-intact did not
trials.failure_mode: STK11/KEAP1 subpopulation diluted by unselected enrollment
trials.notes: GLB trial #4. QUARANTINED — delta +0.366 (patent) vs. +0.2641 (receipt) — vector version unresolved. CT-03 blocker. LATIFY preliminary label applied per 8D remediation 2026-04-28.

trials.drug: Ceralasertib (ATR inhibitor) + olaparib (PARPi)
trials.primary_result: NOT STATED in patent MDC
trials.failure_mode: Patient B vector not defined — delta cannot be computed
trials.blocker: BLOCKED_ENGINEERING — patient B vector not defined (CT-04)
trials.notes: ATR/DDR program trial #5. NOT in GLB set. Delta MISSING — CT-04 blocker. NCT02264678 was split from NCT02264678 per 8D remediation 2026-04-28.

trials.drug: Tusamitamab ravtansine (SAR408701) — anti-CEACAM5 ADC, DM4 payload
trials.indication: 2L+ advanced nonsquamous NSCLC, CEACAM5 IHC ≥2+ in ≥50% of cells
trials.primary_result: PFS HR 1.14 (95% CI 0.86–1.51; P=0.8204). Median PFS 5.4 vs. 5.9 months (docetaxel). Numerically inferior.
trials.failure_mode: CEACAM5 IHC prognostic not predictive; archived tissue limitation; threshold set too low (≥80% subgroup showed directional benefit)
trials.notes: GLB trial #5. Phase 3 failure. Docetaxel arm overperformed historical benchmarks (PFS 5.9 vs. 2.0–4.2 months historical). OS HR 0.85 (P=0.112) — directional but not significant.

trials.drug: Precemtabart tocentecan (M9140) — anti-CEACAM5 ADC, exatecan (Topo1i) payload, β-glucuronide linker
trials.primary_result: Confirmed ORR 7.5% (3/40); unconfirmed 15.0% (6/40). mPFS 5.9 months (95% CI 4.6–7.2). All confirmed responses at doses ≥2.4 mg/kg.
trials.key_biomarker: None identified — CEACAM5 IHC not predictive (Spearman rho = −0.14, P=0.4)
trials.failure_mode: No predictive biomarker identified; D2 gap for Phase 3 enrichment strategy undefined
trials.notes: Merck KGaA. KRAS/NRAS/BRAF mutation status does not predict response. Phase 3 planned Q2/Q3 2026. MTD 2.8 mg/kg Q3W.

trials.drug: Labetuzumab govitecan — anti-CEACAM5 ADC, SN-38 (irinotecan metabolite) payload
trials.indication: 3L+ relapsed/refractory mCRC, all patients had prior irinotecan
trials.primary_result: ORR 1.2% (1/86 confirmed PR). mPFS 3.6 months. mOS 6.9 months. Clinical benefit rate (PR+SD≥4mo) 29%.
trials.key_biomarker: Serum CEA >5 ng/mL (eligibility only); serum CEA predicted PFS/OS in exploratory analysis
trials.failure_mode: SN-38 payload = same mechanism as prior irinotecan therapy; D1 biology failure (resistance pre-established)
trials.notes: Immunomedics. 86 patients, median 5 prior therapies. 38% showed tumor reduction without RECIST response. No Phase 3 initiated.

trials.drug: Cibisatamab (CEA-TCB, CEA/CEACAM5-directed CD3 T-cell engaging bispecific) + FAP-4-1BBL (FAP-targeted 4-1BB ligand)
trials.primary_result: Confirmed ORR 13.5% (7/52; 95% CI 6–26). DCR 50.0%. CRS 57.7% (grade ≥3: 3.8%). Diarrhea 55.8%, colitis 13.5%.
trials.key_biomarker: CEA IHC H-score (predicts DCR); CEACAM5 RNA-seq NOT predictive
trials.failure_mode: Pharmacodynamic immune activation confirmed but ORR 13.5% only; on-target/off-tumor GI toxicity (CEA on normal GI epithelium)
trials.notes: Roche. CEACAM5 selection criterion removed mid-trial after 11 patients. Liver metastases: partial mitigation of immune suppression observed. Fatal CMV colitis (1 patient). Responses in CMS2/immune-excluded tumors.

trials.drug: Tusamitamab sonditecan — anti-CEACAM5 ADC, Topo1i payload, VKG linker (same antibody as CARMEN-LC03)
trials.status: ON HOLD in EU (France, Spain, Sweden, Netherlands) — 2026
trials.primary_result: EU clinical hold — no efficacy data published
trials.failure_mode: D8 Systemic — EU regulatory hold; shared VKG linker + Topo1i chemistry with discontinued PF-08046044 (terminated for toxicity)
trials.data_status: PROVISIONAL — EU clinical trials registry; no peer-reviewed data on hold reason
trials.notes: Seagen/Pfizer. Same antibody as CARMEN-LC03 (tusamitamab). VKG linker + Topo1i shared with discontinued PF-08046044. Competitor: Merck KGaA PROCEADE-CRC-01 advancing to Phase 3.

trials.drug: Adenoviral CEA vaccine + avelumab (anti-PD-L1) + mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab
trials.primary_result: TERMINATED for futility. PFS HR 1.061 (95% CI 0.380–2.966) p=0.91
trials.failure_mode: CEA-specific T cells generated but functionally suppressed in TME; PD-L1 blockade insufficient to rescue vaccine-primed T cells in MSS CRC
trials.notes: Most structurally similar to BreAK CRC-001. mFOLFOX6+bev backbone. Vaccine + CPI + chemo design. Key differentiator: STC-1010 uses DNFB haptenation (ICD mechanism) vs. AdCEA single antigen; BreAK CRC-001 does NOT include a CPI.

trials.drug: Personalized neoantigen vaccine (ChAd68 + saRNA) + nivolumab + ipilimumab + FP + bevacizumab (maintenance)
trials.status: INTERIM — company filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy Oct 2024
trials.primary_result: HR 0.73 (90% CI 0.44–1.21); CI crosses 1.0; data immature
trials.failure_mode: Neoantigen-specific T cells generated but insufficient for PFS benefit in unselected MSS CRC; low ctDNA subgroup HR 0.50 (exploratory)
trials.notes: Gritstone bio. ctDNA-low subgroup HR 0.50 (90% CI 0.20–1.28) — exploratory, CI crosses 1.0. Bankruptcy Oct 2024. Maintenance-phase vaccine concept.

trials.drug: Allogeneic whole-cell vaccine (GVAX) + low-dose cyclophosphamide + pembrolizumab
trials.primary_result: ORR 0% (0/22 evaluable)
trials.failure_mode: Peripheral T-cell induction does not translate to tumor regression; TME suppression prevents effector function at tumor site
trials.notes: Most mechanistically similar to STC-1010 (allogeneic whole-cell vaccine). ORR 0% despite confirmed T-cell responses. Key lesson: pharmacodynamic immune activation ≠ clinical benefit in MSS CRC.

trials.drug: Atezolizumab + cobimetinib (MEKi) vs. atezolizumab mono vs. regorafenib
trials.primary_result: OS: atezo+cobi 8.87 mo vs. atezo 7.10 mo vs. rego 8.51 mo; no significant difference
trials.failure_mode: MEK inhibition failed to convert MSS to immunogenic; T-cell infiltration not achieved at scale
trials.notes: Phase III. Definitively closes MEKi immune priming pathway in MSS CRC. Roche/Genentech.

trials.drug: FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab ± atezolizumab
trials.primary_result: ITT PFS HR 0.69 (p=0.0075); pMMR subgroup HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.63–1.17) — NOT significant
trials.failure_mode: pMMR/MSS benefit marginal and not statistically significant; signal exists only in immune-inflamed subgroup (~20-30% of pMMR)
trials.notes: Immunoscore-IC high pMMR subgroup PFS HR ~0.50 (exploratory). Supports immune infiltrate pre-selection hypothesis for BreAK CRC-001.

trials.drug: Durvalumab + tremelimumab + mFOLFOX6
trials.primary_result: Median PFS 8.2 months (95% CI 5.9–8.6); ORR 64.5%; no randomized control arm
trials.failure_mode: Single-arm design; ORR and PFS consistent with FOLFOX alone; no proof of IO contribution
trials.notes: Exact mFOLFOX6 backbone match to BreAK CRC-001. CD8-high + TGF-β-low subgroup showed better outcomes. Key lesson: randomized control arm required to separate IO contribution from backbone.

trials.drug: Durvalumab + tremelimumab + BSC vs. BSC alone
trials.primary_result: OS HR 0.73 (90% CI 0.55–0.97 p=0.07); median OS 6.6 vs. 4.1 months
trials.failure_mode: Broad enrollment diluted signal; pTMB-high rare (~10-15%); liver metastases abolish benefit
trials.notes: GLB trial #6. pTMB ≥28 OS HR 0.34 (90% CI 0.18–0.63); NLM subgroup OS HR ~0.50. Liver metastasis is the critical stratification variable for IO in MSS mCRC. GAP-01 in BreAK CRC-001 directly replicates this design gap.

trials.drug: Pembrolizumab vs. mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI ± bev/cetux
trials.primary_result: PFS HR 0.60; OS HR 0.74. Definitive positive for MSI-H.
trials.why_appendix: MSI-H only — not applicable to 1L MSS CRC frame. Relevant to BreAK CRC-001 Arm 2A-2 context only.

trials.drug: Nivolumab mono; nivo+ipi; MSS cohort enrolled separately
trials.indication: Phase II multi-cohort; MSI-H and MSS cohorts
trials.primary_result: MSS cohort ORR 0% (n=74). MSI-H ORR 31% mono, 55% combo.
trials.why_appendix: MSS cohort ORR 0% is a useful negative control but is monotherapy CPI only.

trials.drug: Regorafenib 80mg + nivolumab 3mg/kg Q2W
trials.indication: Refractory MSS mCRC and gastric cancer
trials.primary_result: CRC cohort (n=24 MSS): ORR 33%, median PFS 6.3 months. All 8 responders had NO liver metastases.
trials.why_appendix: Regorafenib backbone — not relevant to 1L mFOLFOX6 + vaccine design. Liver metastasis lesson is the only applicable element.

trials.drug: Regorafenib 80–120mg + nivolumab 480mg Q4W
trials.primary_result: ORR 7% (5/70). All 5 responders had NO liver metastases. Non-liver-met ORR 22% (n=23).
trials.why_appendix: Regorafenib backbone. Liver metastasis lesson confirmed in Western population.

trials.drug: Regorafenib 80mg + ipilimumab 1mg/kg Q6W + nivolumab 240mg Q2W
trials.primary_result: ORR 27.6% overall; NLM cohort ORR ~40%; liver-met ORR ~5%. Median OS 20 months in NLM cohort.
trials.why_appendix: Regorafenib backbone. Phase I non-randomized. Strongest IO signal in MSS CRC to date but in refractory setting.
trials.notes: NLM subgroup ORR ~40% and OS 20 months is the benchmark for what IO can achieve in non-liver-metastatic MSS CRC.

trials.drug: FP + bevacizumab ± atezolizumab (maintenance after FOLFOX+bev induction)
trials.primary_result: PFS HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.77–1.40) — no benefit. OS HR 0.91 — no benefit. All biomarker subgroups negative.
trials.why_appendix: Maintenance IO after chemo induction — not concurrent. Superseded by MEDITREME (concurrent mFOLFOX6 + IO) in CORE-06.

trials.drug: Pembrolizumab + mFOLFOX7 (Cohort B, 1L) or FOLFIRI (Cohort D, 2L)
trials.primary_result: Cohort B ORR 23% (1L, includes chemo response). Cohort D ORR 7%. No MSS-specific responses attributable to pembrolizumab.
trials.why_appendix: Phase Ib safety/ORR only. No randomized comparison. ORR consistent with chemo alone.

trials.drug: Cabozantinib (MET/VEGFR2/AXL inhibitor) + durvalumab
trials.primary_result: ORR 27.6% (8/29 evaluable). Median OS 9.1 months. Post-hoc: patients without liver metastases showed higher ORR.
trials.why_appendix: Cabozantinib backbone — not relevant to mFOLFOX6 + vaccine design. Small n.

trials.drug: Multi-peptide TAA vaccine (7 antigens) + Montanide + maintenance chemo
trials.primary_result: T-cell responses to ≥1 antigen in 100% of patients. No objective responses. Stable disease in 5/11.
trials.why_appendix: No mFOLFOX6 backbone. Maintenance setting. Small n.

trials.drug: GVAX + guadecitabine (DNMT inhibitor)
trials.primary_result: No significant increase in CD45RO+ T cells. No clinical responses.
trials.why_appendix: No mFOLFOX6 backbone. Epigenetic priming strategy — not directly relevant to STC-1010 design.

trials.drug: Poxviral vaccine (PANVAC) ± dendritic cells modified with PANVAC
trials.primary_result: No significant OS benefit (n=74). T-cell responses in >70% of patients.
trials.why_appendix: Adjuvant setting — not metastatic. Poxviral platform — different from whole-cell haptenated vaccine.

trials.drug: ELI-002 2P (amphiphile-modified KRAS G12D/G12R peptides + CpG adjuvant)
trials.primary_result: 3/5 CRC patients achieved ctDNA clearance or reduction. Strong mKRAS-specific T-cell responses.
trials.why_appendix: Minimal residual disease setting — not metastatic. Only 5 CRC patients.

trials.drug: Pexastimogene devacirepvec (JX-594) + durvalumab ± tremelimumab
trials.primary_result: ORR 0% (0/21 evaluable). Viral replication confirmed. Increased CD8+ infiltration in some biopsies.
trials.why_appendix: Oncolytic virus platform — different from whole-cell haptenated vaccine. Refractory setting.

trials.drug: Bintrafusp alfa (anti-PD-L1/TGF-β trap bifunctional)
trials.primary_result: ORR 0% in CRC cohort (n=30). TGF-β pathway suppression confirmed.
trials.why_appendix: No vaccine component. No mFOLFOX6 backbone.

trials.drug: Zanzalintinib (XL092, VEGFR/MET/AXL TKI) + atezolizumab vs. regorafenib
trials.primary_result: ONGOING — results pending
trials.why_appendix: Results not yet available. Refractory setting.

trials.drug: mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab → FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (maintenance)
trials.primary_result: mPFS 9.8 months (95% CI 9.0–10.5); ORR 50%; mOS 22.5 months
trials.comparability: HIGH — Best available benchmark for RAS-enriched mFOLFOX6+bev population
trials.notes: Cremolini C et al. Lancet Oncol 2020. 64% RAS-mutant. BRAF-mutant 10% (excluded from BreAK CRC-001). MSI-H 5%. Maintenance phase included in PFS.

trials.drug: mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab
trials.indication: RAS-mutant; unresectable colorectal liver-limited metastases; single Chinese institution
trials.primary_result: mPFS 9.5 months; ORR 54.5%; mOS 25.7 months
trials.comparability: MODERATE-HIGH — Most molecularly aligned benchmark (RAS-mutant required). Liver-limited disease only.
trials.notes: Tang W et al. JCO 2020. Liver-limited disease only — more favorable prognosis. Single Chinese institution. Surgical conversion primary endpoint.

trials.drug: FOLFOX4 + bevacizumab
trials.primary_result: mPFS ~9.4 months (HR 0.83 vs. FOLFOX4+placebo); ORR ~38%; mOS 21.0 months
trials.comparability: MODERATE — Established regulatory benchmark. FOLFOX4 not mFOLFOX6; no RAS/BRAF stratification; enrolled 2003-2005.
trials.notes: Saltz LB et al. JCO 2008. Enrolled 2003-2005 — temporal drift. Unselected population includes ~40-50% RAS wild-type patients excluded from BreAK CRC-001.

trials.drug: FOLFOX4 until progression
trials.indication: Unresectable mCRC; unselected; French multicenter; enrolled 2000-2003
trials.primary_result: mPFS ~9.0 months; ORR ~58.5%; mOS ~19.4 months
trials.comparability: LOW-MODERATE — Historical floor for FOLFOX backbone activity. No bevacizumab; FOLFOX4 not mFOLFOX6; enrolled 2000-2003.
trials.notes: Tournigand C et al. JCO 2006. Historical floor only. No bevacizumab.

trials.drug: mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab
trials.indication: Unresectable mCRC; unselected; Japanese multicenter; enrolled 2010-2013
trials.primary_result: mPFS ~11.7 months; ORR ~64%; mOS ~31.4 months
trials.comparability: LOW-MODERATE — Japanese population; higher OS likely reflects patient selection and post-progression treatment access differences.
trials.notes: Yamazaki K et al. Ann Oncol 2016. Japanese population — OS 31.4 months substantially higher than Western trials. No RAS/BRAF stratification.

trials.drug: mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab + AdCEA vaccine + avelumab vs. SOC alone
trials.primary_result: NEGATIVE PRECEDENT — HR 1.061 (favoring control arm)
trials.comparability: DESIGN REFERENCE ONLY — NOT AN EFFICACY BENCHMARK
trials.notes: Also appears as CORE-01. Listed here as design precedent in historical comparator pack. Do not use as efficacy benchmark.

trials.drug: STC-1010 (DNFB-haptenated whole-cell vaccine) + low-dose cyclophosphamide + GM-CSF + mFOLFOX6 ± bevacizumab
critical_gaps: GAP-01 (CRITICAL): Liver metastasis not pre-specified as stratification variable
GAP-03 (MEDIUM): io=0.40 (moderate) — STC-1010 mechanism requires io≥0.50 for optimal alignment
GAP-04 (HIGH): No biomarker gate for patient selection
trials.notes: Anchor program. Alzeeb et al. 2024 (DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2024.1427428) is the key scientific anchor. PATH A score 0.6944 (canonical_vectors.py). KG v2 value 0.6944 RETIRED 2026-07-05..

trials.analysis_type: Paired primary/recurrent bulk RNA-seq — EMT escape marker analysis
trials.closure_reason: ZEB1 DOWN (delta=-0.34, p=0.000184) at recurrence — opposite of expected escape direction. All canonical EMT markers null or down. EMT upregulation hypothesis NOT supported in bulk GBM.
trials.permanent_boundary: Bulk GBM recurrence under Stupp treatment does not show ZEB1, SOX2, or EMT-panel upregulation in paired primary/recurrent RNA-seq data.
trials.if_revisited: Target ZEB2, TWIST2, or SNAI2 — not ZEB1. Requires single-cell or spatial resolution.
trials.data_status: VERIFIED — GLASS 2025-09-30 release, N=123 Stupp pairs
trials.notes: GLASS syn17038081 is the primary, high-confidence dataset. ZEB1 DOWN is a real signal (p=0.000184, Cohen's d=-0.31), not noise. Three mechanistic explanations: (1) subclonal EMT diluted in bulk, (2) microenvironmental remodeling, (3) alternative resistance mechanism. Cannot distinguish without single-cell/spatial data.

trials.dataset_name: GSE222515 Bulk RNA-seq — GBM Recurrence (directional support)
trials.analysis_type: Bulk RNA-seq — ZEB1/SOX2 directional support analysis
trials.n_pairs: Small recurrent GBM cohort (exact N not confirmed at GLASS rigor level)
trials.closure_reason: Directionally consistent with GLASS (ZEB1 DOWN). Lower confidence — no paired Wilcoxon, no per-gene EMT panel, no file-size/header confirmation at GLASS rigor level. Survival data absent from GEO.
trials.permanent_boundary: Supports GLASS finding directionally but does not independently confirm at GLASS-level evidence quality.
trials.notes: GSE222515 result produced by prior agent run without same artifact-level rigor as GLASS. Use as directional support only, not independent replication.

trials.analysis_type: snRNA-seq paired primary/recurrent — tumor-cell EMT escape analysis

key_results.partial_MES_shift: VIM/FN1/HIF1A UP in 6/8 patients — ZEB1-independent mesenchymal shift present

trials.closure_reason: ZEB1 NULL in tumor cells (delta=-0.076, p=0.742, d=-0.07). EMT score UP but not significant (p=0.461). Partial mesenchymal shift (VIM/FN1/HIF1A) present in 6/8 patients but ZEB1-independent. ZEB1 as escape marker not confirmed at single-cell resolution.
trials.permanent_boundary: ZEB1 is not a confirmed GBM recurrence escape marker at single-cell resolution in Stupp-treated patients (N=8 pairs, 12,189 tumor cells).
trials.if_revisited: Partial MES shift (VIM/FN1/HIF1A) is a real signal — investigate ZEB2, TWIST2, SNAI2 as alternative EMT drivers. Larger N required (N=8 is underpowered for subclonal analysis).
trials.data_status: VERIFIED — GSE174554 snRNA-seq, N=8 tumor-cell pairs, 12,189 tumor cells
trials.notes: Tumor fraction: primary 34.7%, recurrent 28.0% — dilution artifact NOT confirmed. N=8 pairs is underpowered for subclonal EMT detection. Partial MES shift is the most actionable finding: VIM/FN1/HIF1A UP in 6/8 patients suggests ZEB1-independent mesenchymal transition at recurrence.
